focus: reporting-verb stress (admitted, denied, insisted) · weak 'to' in reported commands · reported questions without inversion · 'whether' /ˈweðə/ · attitude in the reporting verb
focus_ar: نبر أفعال النقل (admitted, denied, insisted)، و'to' الخفيفة في الأوامر المنقولة، والأسئلة المنقولة بدون قلب، و'whether'، والموقف في فعل النقل
arabic_challenge: At B2 the reporting verb carries the speaker's attitude ('he admitted' vs 'he claimed'), so it must be STRESSED. Arabic learners default to a flat 'he said that', losing the nuance, and they keep question inversion ('he asked where was it') because Arabic word order allows it.

isolation.instructions: The reporting verb is where the meaning lives, so stress it: 'he adMITted', 'she deNIED', 'they inSISTed'. Each carries a different attitude. Don't bury them.
isolation.instructions_ar: فعل النقل هو موضع المعنى، فانبره: 'he adMITted'، 'she deNIED'. كل واحد يحمل موقفًا مختلفًا.

sentence_practice: He admitted that he was wrong.
daily_drills.record_this: He finally admitted that he had been completely wrong. She firmly denied taking any of the money. They insisted on paying for the whole meal themselves.
daily_drills.self_check: Say 'he admitted that he was wrong'. Is 'adMITted' clearly stressed on the second syllable?

isolation.instructions: Commands become 'told/asked + person + tə + verb': 'she told me tə WAIT', 'he asked us tə LEAVE'. The 'to' is weak /tə/; the action verb takes the stress.
isolation.instructions_ar: الأوامر تصبح 'told/asked + شخص + tə + فعل': 'she told me tə WAIT'. الـ to خفيفة والفعل منبور.

sentence_practice: She told me to wait outside.
He asked us to leave quietly.
They warned me not to go alone.
daily_drills.record_this: She told me to wait outside until she called. He politely asked us to leave the room quietly. They warned me not to go there alone after dark.
daily_drills.self_check: Say 'she told me to wait'. Is 'to' a quick weak /tə/ with 'WAIT' stressed?

isolation.instructions: Reported questions drop the inversion and the question tone: 'He asked where the station WAS ↘' — statement order, falling pitch. It is no longer a question.
isolation.instructions_ar: الأسئلة المنقولة تفقد القلب ونبرة السؤال: 'He asked where the station WAS ↘' — ترتيب خبري ونبرة هابطة.
practice: he asked where the station WAS ↘

pair: he asked where the station was ✅
he asked where was the station ❌
she asked if I was ready ✅

sentence_practice: He asked where the station was.
She asked what I wanted for dinner.
They asked why I was late.
daily_drills.record_this: He asked me where the nearest station was. She asked what I wanted for dinner this evening. They asked why I was so late to the meeting yesterday.
daily_drills.self_check: Say 'he asked where the station was'. Is the word order a statement, with a falling tone?

isolation.instructions: 'whether' (= if) is /ˈweðə/, identical to 'weather' in most accents, with a voiced /ð/. Use it for reported yes/no questions and choices: 'asked whether I'd COME'.
isolation.instructions_ar: 'whether' (= if) تُلفظ /ˈweðə/ بنفس نطق 'weather' مع /ð/ مجهورة، وتُستخدم للأسئلة المنقولة نعم/لا.

sentence_practice: She asked whether or not we agreed.
daily_drills.record_this: He asked whether I'd come to the meeting tomorrow. I honestly wondered whether it really mattered at all. She asked whether or not we actually agreed with the plan.
daily_drills.self_check: Say 'asked whether I'd come'. Is the 'th' a voiced /ð/, sounding just like 'weather'?

target_sounds: conveying attitude through the reporting verb

isolation.instructions: Change the reporting verb and you change the whole meaning — so match your TONE to it. 'He claimed...' said with slight scepticism; 'he admitted...' with weight; 'she boasted...' with a lift.
isolation.instructions_ar: تغيير فعل النقل يغيّر المعنى كله، فاجعل نبرتك تناسبه: claimed بشكّ، admitted بثقل، boasted برفعة.

sentence_practice: He claimed he'd never seen her before.
She admitted she'd made a mistake.
They announced they were getting married.
daily_drills.record_this: He claimed he'd never seen her before in his life, though nobody believed him. She quietly admitted that she'd made a serious mistake. They proudly announced that they were getting married in the spring.
daily_drills.self_check: Say 'he claimed...' then 'she admitted...'. Does your tone change to match each attitude?

challenge_sentences: He admitted that he'd been wrong.
She told me to wait outside.
They asked where the station was.
I wondered whether it really mattered.
daily_drills.record_this: He finally admitted that he'd been completely wrong about it. She told me to wait outside until she was ready. They asked me where the nearest station was. I genuinely wondered whether any of it really mattered.
daily_drills.self_check: Three checks: stressed reporting verb, weak 'to' in commands, and statement order with falling tone in reported questions.

test_yourself.instructions: Record yourself reporting a disagreement, using varied reporting verbs to show each person's attitude. Then listen back and check each feature.
test_yourself.instructions_ar: سجّل نفسك تنقل خلافًا حدث، مستخدمًا أفعال نقل متنوعة تُظهر موقف كل شخص، وبعدين اسمع وراجع.
test_yourself.passage: Let me tell you what happened at the meeting yesterday. The manager announced that the deadline had been moved forward, and asked whether we could finish by Thursday. My colleague immediately complained that it was impossible, and insisted that we needed at least another week. The manager denied that the change was his decision and claimed the client had demanded it. Someone asked why nobody had warned us earlier. He admitted that he'd known for several days but explained that he hadn't wanted to worry anyone. Then he told us to prioritise the main report and asked us not to start anything new. Finally he promised he'd speak to the client again, and suggested we meet on Friday to review progress. Honestly, I wondered whether anything would actually change.

sounds_to_check.stressed reporting verbs: anNOUNCED, comPLAINED, inSISTed, deNIED, CLAIMED, adMITted, exPLAINED, PROMised, sugGESTed
sounds_to_check.reported commands + weak 'to': told us tə prioritise, asked us not tə start
sounds_to_check.reported questions (no inversion, fallin: asked whether we could finish, asked why nobody had warned us
sounds_to_check.'whether' /ˈweðə/: asked whether we could finish, wondered whether anything would change
sounds_to_check.attitude matching: denied/claimed slightly sceptical; admitted weighty; promised warm

scoring_guide.90_100: Reporting verbs stressed and coloured, weak 'to', no inversion. Ready for week 9.
scoring_guide.50_69: Everything reported as 'said that', or inversion kept in questions. Repeat days 1-3.
scoring_guide.below_50: Redo days 1-5, stressing the reporting verb and using statement order.

for_arabic_speakers: At B2 the reporting verb carries the attitude — stress it, and let your tone match it.
Reported commands need 'to': 'told me TO wait', with the 'to' weak /tə/.
Reported questions use statement word order and a FALLING tone — they are no longer questions.
'whether' sounds exactly like 'weather' and is used for yes/no questions and choices.
supplementary_notes.recording_requirement: Record the 'record_this' line daily; compare day 7 with day 1.
